name: The Minotaur
origin_myth: Born to Pasiphaë, Queen of Crete, after she was cursed by Poseidon to fall in love with the Cretan Bull. Imprisoned in Daedalus's Labyrinth until slain by Theseus.
physical_description: Nine-foot-tall creature with the muscular body of a man and the head, horns, and hooves of a colossal bull. Wears tight white briefs in his Book 1 manifestation.
weaknesses: Horns can be snapped off and used as weapons
description: The iconic Cretan bull-man. Percy Jackson defeats him barehanded on Half-Blood Hill in Book 1 by tearing off his horn. He reforms in Tartarus and leads Kronos's vanguard at the Williamsburg Bridge in Book 5.

name: Medusa
origin_myth: Originally a beautiful priestess of Athena who was transformed into a snake-haired Gorgon by Athena after being seduced by Poseidon in Athena's temple.
physical_description: Appears disguised in black veil and abaya as a Middle Eastern woman. Beneath the veil, she possesses live squirming venomous snakes for hair, fangs, and a face so hideous it turns viewers to stone.
abilities: Petrifying gaze (turns living flesh to stone)
weaknesses: Reflective surfaces (can be viewed safely via mirror or polished shield)
notable_victims: Countless mortals turned to garden statues
disguise_form: Aunty Em, owner of Aunty Em's Garden Gnome Emporium
description: The mortal Gorgon sister. Runs a statue emporium in New Jersey under the alias Aunty Em. Decapitated by Percy Jackson using his polished bronze cell phone reflection and Riptide. Her head is mailed to Olympus and later used by Sally Jackson to petrify Gabe Ugliano.

name: Alecto
origin_myth: One of the three Erinyes (Furies) born from the blood of Ouranos when he was castrated by Kronos. Serves Hades as minister of vengeance and Underworld tormentor.
physical_description: Disguised as a leather-jacket-wearing algebra teacher at Yancy Academy. True form is a hideous hag with bat wings, yellow eyes, fangs, and a whip dripping with molten fire.
notable_victims: Tormented souls in Fields of Punishment
disguise_form: Mrs. Dodds, Yancy Academy math teacher
description: Head of the three Furies and faithful lieutenant of Hades. Attacks Percy at the Metropolitan Museum in Chapter 1 of Book 1 disguised as Mrs. Dodds. Later escorting Percy and Nico in the Underworld in Book 5.

name: Echidna
origin_myth: Ancient half-woman, half-snake mother of Greek mythology's most horrific beasts (Cerberus, Hydra, Chimera, Nemean Lion).
physical_description: Appears as a rotund, heavy-set woman in a denim dress carrying a Chihuahua in a handbag. True form reveals a scaly snake body from the waist down and reptile eyes.
notable_victims: Percy Jackson (poisoned at St. Louis Arch)
disguise_form: Overweight tourist woman carrying a Chihuahua bag
description: The Mother of All Monsters. Corner Percy, Annabeth, and Grover at the top of the St. Louis Arch in Book 1, loosing her son the Chimera against Percy.

name: Chimera
origin_myth: Spawn of Echidna and Typhon, famous for terrorizing Lycia until slain by Bellerophon riding Pegasus.
physical_description: Initially disguised as a harmless Chihuahua. Transforms into a ten-foot beast with the head and mane of a lion, body of a goat, and a ten-foot venomous serpent tail.
weaknesses: Lead or metal swallowed during fire breathing
notable_victims: Percy Jackson (poisoned tail strike in Book 1)
description: Fire-breathing hybrid monster. Poisoned Percy Jackson with its tail at the St. Louis Arch, forcing Percy to leap into the Mississippi River.

name: Procrustes
origin_myth: Rogue giant son of Poseidon who ambushed travelers on the road to Athens and stretched or chopped them to fit his iron beds until stopped by Theseus.
physical_description: Seven-foot tall, ugly giant running 'Crusty's Waterbed Palace' in West Hollywood. Has greyish skin, slicked hair, and wears a leisure suit.
abilities: Magical bed trapping (snaps cords to bind victims)
weaknesses: Easily tricked into lying on his own beds
notable_victims: Annabeth Chase and Grover Underwood (trapped on beds in Book 1)
disguise_form: Crusty, waterbed salesman in West Hollywood
description: The Stretcher giant. Guards the secret entrance to the Underworld in West Hollywood. Tricked by Percy into lying on one of his own beds, where Percy decapitates him.

name: Cerberus
origin_myth: Three-headed giant hound offspring of Echidna and Typhon stationed at the gates of Erebos to prevent the dead from escaping.
physical_description: Massive three-headed hound twice the size of a rhinoceros, with a serpent tail and razor-sharp teeth.
weaknesses: Red rubber ball / Playing fetch (pacified by Annabeth)
description: The giant three-headed guard dog of Hades. Pacified by Annabeth Chase using a red rubber ball from Waterland, allowing the quest group to pass safely into Erebos.

name: Polyphemus
origin_myth: Son of Poseidon and the nymph Thoosa. Famous for capturing Odysseus in his cave before being blinded by a sharpened olive stake.
physical_description: Colossal fifteen-foot blind Cyclops with a milky, scarred single eye socket, wearing sheepskins and wielding a massive tree-trunk club.
abilities: Acute sense of smell and hearing
description: The blind Cyclops guardian of the Golden Fleece on his island in the Sea of Monsters. Traps Grover (mistaking him for a female Cyclops) and Clarisse before being outwitted by Percy and Annabeth.

name: Lernean Hydra
origin_myth: Ancient serpent beast of Lerna slain by Heracles as his Second Labor.
physical_description: Nine-headed reptilian swamp monster with acid-spitting heads and venomous blood.
abilities: Multiplication (grows two heads for every head severed)
description: Nine-headed dragon monster encountered by Percy, Annabeth, Tyson, and Clarisse at a Monster Donut shop in Florida. Obliterated by Clarisse's CSS Birmingham cannon fire.

name: Scylla
origin_myth: Once a nymph transformed by Circe into a six-headed sea monster occupying a cliff opposite Charybdis.
physical_description: Six long serpentine necks extending from a cliff cave, each ending in a reptilian head with triple rows of shark teeth.
abilities: Lightning-fast lunges to scoop sailors from ship decks
notable_victims: Six sailors from Clarisse's Confederate ironclad ship
description: Six-headed cliff monster in the Sea of Monsters. Plucks six zombie sailors off Clarisse's ironclad vessel as they navigate the strait.

name: Charybdis
origin_myth: Nymph daughter of Poseidon turned into a colossal whirlpool sea monster by Zeus.
physical_description: Giant underwater maw with slimy teeth and iron braces, creating a massive whirlpool three times a day.
abilities: Sucking entire ships into her gullet and spitting out flaming debris
description: Colossal whirlpool monster opposite Scylla. Destroys Clarisse's ironclad ship CSS Birmingham by overheating its boilers.

name: Dr. Thorn
origin_myth: Persian and Greek myth beast with a human face, lion body, and scorpion tail capable of shooting poisonous spikes.
physical_description: Disguised as Vice Principal Dr. Thorn at Westover Hall (heterochromatic eyes: one blue, one brown). True form is a lion-like monster with a scorpion tail shooting iron spikes.
disguise_form: Dr. Thorn, Vice Principal at Westover Hall
description: Manticore serving Kronos. Ambushes Percy, Thalia, Annabeth, and Grover at Westover Hall to kidnap Bianca and Nico di Angelo. Knocks Annabeth off a cliff before being driven off by the Hunters of Artemis.

name: The Nemean Lion
origin_myth: Vicious lion with impenetrable golden fur slain by Heracles as his First Labor.
physical_description: Colossal lion with glittering golden pelt and steel-sharp claws.
abilities: Invulnerable golden hide (reflects all blades, arrows, and weapons)
description: Invulnerable lion deployed by Luke at the National Air and Space Museum. Defeated when Percy, Zoë, and Grover force astronaut freeze-dried food into its mouth, causing it to gag and exposing its soft throat to Percy's blade. Percy claims its pelt as a protective coat.

name: Erymanthian Boar
origin_myth: Gigantic wild boar that terrorized Arcadia until captured alive by Heracles.
physical_description: Thirty-foot-tall wild boar with pink skin, tusks as large as canoes, and reeking of sewage.
description: Giant boar summoned by Grover's pan pipes in Cloudcroft, New Mexico. The quest group rides its back across the Southwest into California.

name: Ophiotaurus
origin_myth: Prophetic creature whose entrails, if burned in sacred fire, give the offerer the power to overthrow the gods.
physical_description: Sea creature with the head and torso of a black calf and the long scaly tail of a serpent.
abilities: Granting divine overthrow power if slain and burned
description: Half-cow, half-serpent sea creature rescued by Percy in Long Island Sound and named 'Bessie'. Protected in a water sphere on Mount Olympus to prevent Kronos from burning its entrails.

name: Ladon
origin_myth: Hundred-headed dragon assigned by Hera to guard the Golden Apples in the Garden of the Hesperides.
physical_description: Colossal copper dragon coiled around the Golden Apple tree with one hundred snapping heads, each speaking with different voices.
notable_victims: Zoë Nightshade (mortally poisoned by his bite in Book 3)
description: The hundred-headed dragon guarding Mount Tamalpais. Inflicts a fatal poisonous wound on Zoë Nightshade during the quest to free Artemis.

name: Kampê
origin_myth: Monstrous dragon-woman appointed by Kronos to guard the Cyclopes and Hekatonkheires in Tartarus until slain by Zeus during the Titanomachy.
physical_description: Terrifying woman's torso with dragon wings, a serpent body below, fifty animal heads sprouting from her waist, and venomous whip swords.
weaknesses: Crushed under massive volleys of boulders
description: Fearsome ancient jailer of Tartarus guarding Briares in Alcatraz. Slain during the Battle of the Labyrinth when Briares crushes her under a barrage of boulders.

name: Kelli
origin_myth: Vampiric demon daughter of Hecate with one bronze leg and one donkey leg, seducing young men to drink their blood.
physical_description: Disguised as a blonde cheerleader at Goode High. True form reveals fiery hair, fangs, one donkey leg, and one leg forged of bronze.
description: Lead Empousa demon serving Kronos. Ambushes Percy at Goode High orientation before being stabbed from behind by Annabeth Chase.

name: Geryon
origin_myth: Three-bodied giant who owned a herd of red cattle on Erytheia until slain by Heracles as his Tenth Labor.
physical_description: Giant with three attached human chests, one set of legs, wearing three matching western shirts.
abilities: Three hearts (survives single torso chest wounds)
weaknesses: An arrow shot sideways through all three hearts simultaneously
notable_victims: Nico di Angelo (captured at Triple G Ranch)
disguise_form: Ranch owner in cowboy hat and boots
description: Three-chested giant operating Triple G Ranch in Texas. Slain by Percy Jackson who shoots an arrow guided by the wind through all three of his chests at once.

name: Typhon
origin_myth: The deadliest monster of Greek mythology, born to Gaea and Tartarus to destroy Olympus after the Titanomachy.
physical_description: Colossal storm giant towering into the clouds with a human upper body, snake legs, dark hurricane clouds for hair, and eyes flashing lightning.
abilities: Generating megatsunamis, volcanic eruptions, and country-spanning tornadoes
weaknesses: Chained under Mount Saint Helens / Poseidon's water forces pushing him into Tartarus abyss
notable_victims: Multiple Olympian gods wounded during his cross-country rampage
description: The Father of All Monsters. Awakened by the Mount St. Helens eruption in Book 4, he marches across America in Book 5, occupying all twelve Olympians until Poseidon and the Cyclopes drag him into Tartarus.

name: Lydian Drakon
origin_myth: Ancient giant serpent monster foretold to be slain only by a child of Ares.
physical_description: Two-hundred-foot long giant serpent with green chitinous scales, yellow eyes, and spitting corrosive acid.
abilities: Scales impervious to all weapons except an Ares demigod
weaknesses: Prophesied vulnerability to a child of Ares (Clarisse La Rue)
description: Massive drakon unleashed in Manhattan. Kills Silena Beauregard before Clarisse La Rue arrives in a divine Ares rage, spearing it through the eye.

name: Cacus
origin_myth: Fire-breathing giant son of Hephaestus who lived in a cave on Mount Aventine until slain by Heracles.
physical_description: Fifteen-foot fire-breathing giant wearing a counterfeit designer warm-up suit.
description: Fire-breathing giant who steals Hermes's caduceus in 'The Staff of Serapis' / 'The Demigod Files'. Slain by Percy Jackson and Annabeth Chase.
